attack_mechanism: For a ordinary execution instruction, `exec_done` is produced by the default `(e_state == E_EXEC)` completion arm. An attacker who forces `openMSP430.inst_ad` away from its terminal value can keep the selected predicate false on successive `mclk` cycles. `openMSP430.inst_ad` sets the selected completion class, execution state, or transition into the required terminal state; the intervening RTL assignments are qualified by `openMSP430.frontend_0.dst_acalc`, `openMSP430.frontend_0.exec_jmp`. Decode and fetch remain blocked waiting for completion, creating a persistent loss of instruction retirement. The pertinent register-transfer chain is `openMSP430.inst_ad -> openMSP430.frontend_0.dst_acalc -> openMSP430.frontend_0.e_state_nxt -> openMSP430.frontend_0.e_state -> openMSP430.frontend_0.exec_done`.
